messages:
Alex W: Heads-up — planning a KEK/key-rollforward across AWS KMS, GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault next Wed 02:00-06:00 PT. Need input on RBAC, audit telemetry, and emergency rollback.
Priya N: TL;DR: keep auto-rotate for low-risk keys, manual rewrap for tenants with regulated PII. Also need a clear playbook if a rewrap job fails mid-tenant.
Matt S: Proposed rollout: canary on dev, quick staging run, 1% of prod traffic, monitor 30m, 10% for 2h, then 100%. Automate fail-open to previous key on >=3 rewrap errors.
Sasha K: RBAC notes: create a dedicated role `key-rewrappers` with narrow permissions. AWS: `kms:ReEncrypt*` and `kms:DescribeKey`; GCP: `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt`, `cloudkms.cryptoKeys.get`; Azure: `Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/*/wrapKey/action` (we should verify exact scope). Grant via short-lived principals and require MFA for ad hoc manual rewraps.
Alex W: Audit requirements — every rewrap must include who started it, source IP, job id, old_key_id/new_key_id, start/end timestamps and per-object status. sec-telemetry should emit structured events.
Priya N: Example Kibana/ES query to find rewrap failures: `event.type: "kms_reencrypt" AND job.type: "rewrap" AND status: "error"` — include `user.identity` in results. Add a dashboard tile for error rate and average latency per tenant.
Sasha K: Backwards compatibility: runtime must accept both v1 and v2 ciphertext headers. Plan: add `ciphertext_header.version` field and `key_id` in metadata. On decrypt path, if header missing, treat as v1; log deprecation once per-ciphertext.
Matt S: Emergency scenario: if CVE or key compromise is detected (e.g., hypothetical CVE-2025-9999 affecting wrap libraries), immediate steps: 1) revoke KEK, 2) spin new KEK, 3) pause non-essential writes, 4) run prioritized manual rewrap for highest-risk tenants, 5) alert compliance and legal.
Alex W: For staged rewrap jobs we need idempotency and resume support. Jobs should be resumable per-tenant and per-shard; keep a job checkpoint doc in our DB with `processed_count`, `failed_count`, `last_ciphertext_id`.
Sasha K: Ops runbook snippet for manual AWS rewrap (example):
```
aws kms reencrypt \\\n  --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin \\\n  --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111:key/NEW-KEY-ID \
  --destination-encryption-context '{"tenant":"tenant-123"}' \
  outputfileb://ct_rewrapped.bin
```
Note: wrap with encryption context to bind tenant.
Priya N: Observability: emit per-job metrics: `rewrap.duration_ms`, `rewrap.errors`, `rewrap.bytes_processed`, `rewrap.objects_total`. Tag by `tenant_id`, `job_id`, `env`.

oncall-bot: Scheduled window confirmed for 1971234567-job-rotate starting 1971235200 — will post start/finish events.
sec-bot: Reminder: require JIT approval for role `key-rewrappers` during the rollout. Use ephemeral tokens if possible.
Matt S: Timing: prefer Thu/Friday low traffic. Ops estimate: full-prod run ~6-8 hours depending on caching and batching. Non-blocking workloads can be backgrounded.
Alex W: Questions for infra: can the runtime support streaming rewrap (prefix-based) to reduce KV cache churn? If not, we'll schedule tenant-by-tenant small batches.
Sasha K: Also: preflight checklist — RBAC created and audited, audit pipelines indexed, canary tenant snapshot taken, rollback key staged and tested, alerting thresholds set (error rate >1% triggers halt).
Priya N: I'll draft the playbook and an incident banner template for customer comms. Also include a legal checklist for regulated tenants.
Alex W: Good. Action items: Priya draft playbook, Matt draft job checkpoint schema, Sasha create RBAC perms and test in dev, I'll coordinate timing with product and oncall. Ping me in #eng-sre when done. :thumbsup:
